author: H. H. Richardson's office (the Archives catalogue names Richardson, Henry Hobson, as creator)
citation: 'Main Entrance Door. House for J. J. Glessner Esq. Chicago Ill.' Sheet No. 95, scale 3/4 in. = 1 ft, black ink on linen tracing cloth, 1885-1887; microfilmed March 1952 from originals lent by the Houghton Library (Burnham Library-University of Illinois microfilm project, roll 16, frame 68). Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson & Burnham Archives, call number 1973 1, mqc 69517. The same sheet's 'Copy', No. 95A, is roll 16, frame 70 (mqc 69194).
describes_date: as designed for the house completed in December 1887
repository: Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson & Burnham Art and Architecture Archives (Archival Image Collection). Prairie library ids a18-rba-mf-glessner-f68-main-entrance-door (frame 68) and a18-rba-mf-glessner-f70 (frame 70); Glessner exterior audit #088 and #090.
locator: The whole sheet: the door leaf in elevation from outside. The frame-70 copy (No. 95A, marked 'Copy') draws the same door line for line. The OTHER No. 95A (frame 69, mqc 69279) draws a floral rosette grille and is endorsed 'Not Correct'; it is not this source and nothing is read from it.
rights_note: An office drawing of 1885-1887, public domain by age; the 1952 microfilm is a mechanical copy of it. The Archives' statement asks that publication be arranged with them, as it does for the Taylor photograph (taylor_2135_glessner_exterior_1887_1889). No pixels are republished or used as textures: only the door's proportions and the arrangement of its parts are read from the sheet.

rights_checked.method: T-2216: read the Archives' catalogue record for mqc 69517 (contentdm singleitem API): 'Rights Information: For publication information please contact the Art Institute of Chicago Archives at archives@artic.edu.'
rights_checked.outcome: public domain by age (an 1885-1887 drawing); proportions read, no pixels republished, as for taylor_2135_glessner_exterior_1887_1889

access_notes: Viewed 2026-10-13 (T-2216) from the Prairie image store's copies of frames 68 and 70, read at 3x on the door. Proportions as shares of the leaf (width from the viewer's left, height from the top): the studded border about 0.085 of the width each side, 0.05 of the height at the top and 0.04 at the foot; the grille's square frame 0.23-0.78 across and 0.13-0.49 down; six upright and six level bars inside it, evenly spaced, each running about 0.035 of the width past the frame to a round knob; the centre three cells across by four down filled, the top row with the house number 1800 and the three rows below with one curled scroll a cell; a strap across the leaf at 0.56 down, from 0.06 to 0.93, with a raised boss and knob at its centre and a ring-handled latch plate at its left end; two fielded panels 0.24-0.78 across, at 0.62-0.72 and 0.77-0.87 down; nail-head studs about 0.07 of the height apart down both stiles and along the top and foot; the field's corners and the rail's ends shaped as cusped scrolls, with iron corner pieces.
note: The drawing is a design, so the as-built leaf rests on the agreement of evidence of the built door: an undated photograph of the Prairie front (Prairie library a18-gh-glessner-front-with-keith, probably 1890s-1920s; cited only) shows, on the dark leaf, the figures 1800 at about a fifth of its height and a knob at mid-height, which is where this sheet puts the grille's number row and the strap's boss; HABS (data p. 21) records the front door as oak.
what_it_supplies: the leaf's arrangement: studded border, square iron grille over a strap rail, two fielded panels below
the grille's bar count, its knobbed bar ends and its filled centre with the house number and scrolls
the hardware: the strap, its central boss and knob, the latch plate and ring at the left, the corner irons
every part's position as a share of the leaf's width and height
what_it_does_not_supply: dimensions in feet: the leaf's 4.7 x 7.5 ft is HABS sheet 5's, and the sheet's shares are applied to it
the depth of any member, panel, bar or stud (reconstructed)
the scrolls' or figures' exact forms at a resolution that could be traced (nothing is traced)
